title: SLA-driven intake lanes for hosted chat/streaming/tooling feature requests
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a deterministic intake and routing rubric for Hosted feature requests that involve chat, streaming, tool/function calling, or structured outputs. The goal is to convert inbound enterprise asks into one of four deterministic lanes (Fast Pass SLA, Engineering Triage, Product Backlog, Security/Compliance Review) based on explicit signals (tenant SLAs, PII scope, runtime cost model, structured-output schema needs, integration complexity). Deliverables: intake rubric, onboarding checklist for Sales/Support, automated eligibility filter prototype for the intake form, and rollout plan for Q2 customer onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable intake form mapping to 1 of 4 lanes with >95% deterministic routing on historical sample
Playbook and checklist published in Confluence with examples for chat+toolchains and structured-output contracts
Rollout plan signed off by Sales, Support, Security, and Eng with SLAs and escalation paths
Prototype eligibility filter implemented on the intake form and hooked to Linear creation with correct tags
notes: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with Sales and Solutions Engineering. Captured common ask patterns: multi-step tool chains, streaming telemetry, regulated PII workloads.
2026-02-25: Engineering feasibility review. ENG requested clearer cost-signal (estimated RPS, avg seq length) on intake form.
2026-03-02: Design consult scheduled to create compact intake UI for sales demos; agreed to a progressive disclosure pattern for sensitive fields.
2026-03-06: Security requested additional KMS and data-retention questions for any item flagged as 'Private deployment candidate'.
2026-03-10: Built sample dataset of 280 historical asks from last 12 months to evaluate deterministic rules; initial accuracy 88% before adding tenant SLA and estimated cost fields.
2026-03-12: PM/Eng sync. Decided to implement a 'cost bucket' estimation (Low/Medium/High) on intake to help routing to Dedicated vs Hosted.
2026-03-14: Ready for validation with Sales on 10 live tickets next week; created pilot intake form and automation rules in Linear workflow.
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Keep four lanes (Fast Pass SLA, Eng Triage, Product Backlog, Security Review) after discussion — aligns with support routing and capacity planning.
2026-03-06: Add explicit 'structured-output contract' checkbox to escalate when schema validation or JSON-LD constraints are required.
2026-03-12: Use conservative default routing (prefer Eng Triage) when estimated cost or sequence length is unknown to avoid SLA violations.
2026-03-14: Pilot will run for 2 weeks with Sales-only intake to validate deterministic routing accuracy and false-positive rates.
next_steps: Finalize intake form fields and validation rules with Engineering (due 2026-03-18)
Implement Linear automation to set labels and parent project based on lane (ENG automation ticket ENG-3180)
Run 2-week Sales pilot on ~10 incoming feature asks and record routing accuracy and escalation frequency
